decisions.rationale: Fair value was reached only on the conservative DCF leg; the multiple-discount thesis is intact, quality metrics are stable or improving and no trigger is near. Leverage drift, a guidance cut and a small bearish macro tilt cap conviction at 4, so no ADD; the existing position stays at its size into the Oct 28 results.

Thesis intact: returns, margins and FCF all still rising, no trigger near, valuation still at the 5-year floor. Conviction stays 4, not 5, given AI/free-filing risk to TurboTax and a small bearish macro tilt. The position already sits around its volatility-scaled conviction-4 size, so HOLD rather than ADD.

The blended base fair value is only modestly above the price, and the EV/EBITDA method is below it. The trailing cheapness rests on peak commodity margins with no moat, and results are due within two weeks. Good balance sheet and cash yield, but not compelling: cash is preferred.

Cheap on every own-history multiple with an excellent balance sheet, but the margin surge looks hit-driven, the decline is unexplained and Q3 results are two weeks away. It would also add to existing China-gaming exposure. Good but not compelling: AVOID until results show revenue durability.

Cheap on every multiple, but shipbuilding multiples are lowest at peak margins, the holding-company structure clouds attributable earnings, and the steep drawdown has no explanation in the evidence. That is good but not compelling. Q3 2026 results (around Nov 13, 2026) are the test of whether the margin is structural; cash is acceptable until then.

No durable moat: margins are spot-metal pass-through with falling grades, the normalised fair value sits far below the price, and the primary-weight macro overlay tilts moderately bear. Strong cash and net cash do not offset that. Conviction 2 is below the buy threshold; cash is the better holding.

Quality is outstanding, but earnings are metal-price driven, with a single asset, a new CEO and a moderately bearish macro tilt. The price is well above base fair value and at a large peer premium. That is good but not compelling, so I avoid and hold cash, re-checking at the entry price or if Stage 3 economics prove out.

This is not a quality business on the evidence: it lost money deeply in three of five years, and the TTM profit is likely licensing-driven. The fair value rests only on EV/Revenue of distorted revenue, with rNPV unavailable. Binary clinical and NRDL risks cannot be quantified. Good optionality, not a compelling core position.

Trailing cheapness rests on cyclically high commodity earnings; own-history EV/EBITDA and EV/Sales are near 5y highs and the close sits above the mechanical bull fair value. Macro overlay tilts toward bear, Q3 results land Oct 21, 2026 and BlueNord is unclosed. Good business, not a compelling price: no position, cash preferred.

Quality and balance sheet are excellent and multiples are below their five-year lows, but the research shows no revenue-growth evidence to explain the derating, cash conversion is weakening, shares are diluting, and Q3 results land on Oct 29. Good but not compelling: conviction 3, AVOID, with an entry price at base fair value less the margin of safety.

Quality is rising, the balance sheet is net cash, and even the mechanical bear fair value sits above the price. Single-category weather risk, falling gross margin and added China concentration keep conviction at 4, not 5; standard volatility-scaled core size. Consumer Discretionary stays under the sector cap and holdings well below 15.

Quality is outstanding, but low trailing multiples rest on hit-driven peak earnings, growth is decelerating, FCF conversion is falling and base fair value is below the price. Durability of the IP engine is unproven, so good-not-compelling: AVOID, cash preferred. Re-research nearer the margin-of-safety entry or on evidence of a second franchise.

The drift setup is genuine, but the honest target is the 52-week high of 174.52. Only the mechanical minimum of 180.34 reaches 2:1, and it needs a fresh all-time high in eight weeks from an overbought RSI, at a stretched multiple, with a small bear macro tilt. A trade that is good but not compelling is an AVOID.

The setup qualifies, but the room to the 3-month peak is about 2.4x the stop distance, below the 2.5x rule. The target needs roughly five ATRs in 34 days through falling swing highs, while short interest rises and multiples sit above their 5y max. The plan's reward:risk is only marginal. Conviction 3, so AVOID; cash is acceptable.

Setup qualifies mechanically and the 2:1 plan is arithmetically valid, but the edge is unproven: no visible beat magnitude, partial fade after one session, RSI extended, and multiples above 5-year maximums create gap-down risk on any disappointment. Good but not compelling; cash is acceptable.

Reward:risk meets the minimum only on paper: the target must clear the 198.00 swing high that capped September with no catalyst before January results, while lower lows and negative 3-month relative strength weaken the uptrend edge. Good but not compelling; cash is acceptable.

The setup is valid, but the edge is unclear. The price has gone past the reaction, RSI is 80.2, and the minimum target has no resistance or valuation support for a low-volatility name. Reward:risk passes only mechanically. Good but not compelling, so AVOID; I would revisit on a pullback to the 50-day average.

Drift is real but already stretched (152% of jump held, RSI 69.0) at the 1,379.80 swing high. The ATR stop at 1,228.14 forces a 1,683.72 target, well above the 1,468.70 six-month high; a 2.6% constant-currency grower is unlikely to cover that in 8 weeks. The honest target fails 2:1, so AVOID.

The setup qualifies mechanically, but the honest target is the 55.69-55.70 swing highs or at best the 67.07 52-week high, short of the 68.35 2:1 level from a 46.21 stop. Sales and EPS grew only 1%, EBITDA fell, and price already sits at base fair value. Reward:risk does not hold; cash is preferable.

The reaction day came before the results, and the results showed only marginal growth, so there is no results beat for the price to digest. The entry is overbought at a 6-month high, the 50-day is below the 200-day, and the activist catalyst is binary. A 2:1 plan exists on paper, but its edge is unclear. Cash is preferred.
